newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem guerrillas kill 12 Algerian civilians.
newsitem.headline: Moslem guerrillas kill 12 Algerian civilians.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists killed 12 civilians in Algeria last week in a dispute over stolen cattle, the Algerian El-Watan newspaper reported on Saturday.
El-Watan said two of the civilians were beheaded and the rest shot last Wednesday in the southwestern village of Saida.
Nearly 200 people, most of them civilians in remote villages, have been killed since early November in Algeria, where Moslem rebels are battling security forces.

About 60,000 people have died in the five year conflict that erupted after authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
Last month Algerians voted to change their constitution to legalise political parties but outlaw those based on religion. The FIS has already been banned.
